mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the authorisation logic lets the model invent a Compliance-officer record-read that returns Permitted — exactly the leak LeastPrivilege / FR-007 / FR-019 / FR-008 are meant to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthLogicViolation { some op: Operation | some op.caller and op.caller.role = ComplianceRole and op.kind = OpReadRecord and op.outcome = Permitted }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the audit-per-op fact lets an authenticated access exist with no matching audit entry — the precise SC-002 / FR-013 failure mode.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MissingAudit { some op: Operation | some op.caller and (no ae: AuditEntry | ae.ofOp = op) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the snapshot constraint lets a ClinicalNote carry author_role != clinician — FR-011 / data-model.md author_role CHECK violation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoteRoleSnapshot { some n: ClinicalNote | n.noteAuthorRole = PatientRole }

mutation_targets.rationale: Without the attribution constraint, audit entries may misreport their accessor's role — exactly the FR-014 misattribution we need to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditMisattribution { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.recordedRole != ae.ofOp.caller.role }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the pairing fact lets a non-patient user carry an assigned_record_id, violating the data-model.md paired-CHECK that FR-003 encodes.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NonPatientAssigned { some u: User | u.role = ClinicianRole and some u.assignedRecord }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the matrix declaration removes the hard-deny semantics; an invented model can declare compliance officers as record-readers, which PermissionCompleteness forbids.
